problem:
Compute the following determinant using a cofactor expansion along the $2$nd row:

$$
|\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & 3 & 4 \\ 0 & 2 & 0 & 0 \\ 3 & 0 & 8 & -5 \\ -1 & 1 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}|.
$$
worked_solution:
Using cofactor expansion along the $2$nd row, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & 3 & 4 \\ 0 & 2 & 0 & 0 \\ 3 & 0 & 8 & -5 \\ -1 & 1 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}| & =0\cdot {C}_{21}+2\cdot {C}_{22}+0\cdot {C}_{23}+0\cdot {C}_{24} \\  & =2\cdot (-1)^{2+2}\cdot |\begin{aligned}0 & 3 & 4 \\ 3 & 8 & -5 \\ -1 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =2|\begin{aligned}0 & 3 & 4 \\ 3 & 8 & -5 \\ -1 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, computing the $3\times 3$ determinant by applying a Laplace expansion along the $3$rd row, we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}0 & 3 & 4 \\ 3 & 8 & -5 \\ -1 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}| & =(-1)\cdot {C}_{31}+0\cdot {C}_{32}+0\cdot {C}_{33} \\  & =(-1)\cdot (-1)^{3+1}\cdot |\begin{aligned}3 & 4 \\ 8 & -5\end{aligned}| \\  & =(-1)|\begin{aligned}3 & 4 \\ 8 & -5\end{aligned}| \\  & =(-1)(-15-32) \\  & =(-1)\cdot (-47) \\  & =47\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore,

$$
|\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & 3 & 4 \\ 0 & 2 & 0 & 0 \\ 3 & 0 & 8 & -5 \\ -1 & 1 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}|=2\cdot 47=94.
$$
